issues.t: Automatic transmission slipping or failing
issues.sym: Shifts that slip, flare or come late, a jolt going into gear, or the van refusing to move in drive or reverse. It often starts around 100,000 miles.
issues.why: The four-speed automatic transaxles in the Windstar (the AX4S early on, then the AX4N/4F50N) wear out internally. Transmission failure is the most-reported problem on this van, especially for 2000 and 2003.
issues.next: Check the fluid level and smell right away. If it slips or won't engage, stop driving it hard and get a transmission diagnosis; a rebuilt or used unit is the usual fix.

issues.t: Rear axle cracking from rust (recall)
issues.sym: A clunk or knocking from the rear, the van pulling or wandering, or uneven rear tire wear. In the worst cases the rear axle beam snaps and the van becomes hard to control.
issues.why: On vans driven where roads are salted, rust weakens the rear axle beam until it cracks. Ford recalled these vans several times to inspect the axle and add reinforcing brackets or replace it, and later recalled again because some brackets were installed wrong.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open Ford recalls (10V-385, 12V-193, 12V-195 and 15V-608). If you hear new noises from the rear, have the axle inspected before driving far.

issues.t: Front lower control arm and subframe rust (recall)
issues.sym: Clunking from the front end, loose or wandering steering, or the front wheel sitting out of line after a bump.
issues.why: Road salt corrodes the rear mount of the front lower control arms and the front subframe body mounts. A mount can break loose and cause a sudden loss of steering control.
issues.next: Check for open recalls 11V-030 and 12V-194. If the recall is done or closed, have the subframe and control arm mounts inspected for rust at every tire rotation.

issues.t: Broken front coil springs
issues.sym: A loud bang or clunk from the front over bumps, the front sitting lower on one side, or a tire that suddenly goes flat because a broken spring cut it.
issues.why: The front coil springs on early Windstars rust and snap. Ford extended spring coverage on 1995-1998 vans and ran a safety recall in salt states for 1997-1998 vans because a broken spring could slice the tire.
issues.next: If you hear a bang from the front or the van leans, look at the springs and the inside of the tires. Replace springs in pairs. The old extended coverage has run out, but check for any open recall on your VIN.

issues.t: Head gasket leak and overheating
issues.sym: Coolant disappears, the temperature gauge climbs, white smoke comes from the exhaust, or the oil looks milky. Left alone it can ruin the engine.
issues.why: The 3.8L V6 has a long history of head gasket failures. Ford extended coverage on 1995 Windstars and later issued bulletins for oil getting into the coolant and gasket leaks on later years.
issues.next: Stop driving if it overheats. Have a cooling system pressure test and a combustion gas test done, and check the oil for coolant. Catching it early can save the engine.

issues.t: Intake manifold gasket leak
issues.sym: A check engine light with lean codes (P0171/P0174), rough idle, coolant loss with no visible puddle, or a sweet smell. Coolant can also end up in the oil.
issues.why: The intake manifold gaskets on the 3.8L wear out and start leaking air or coolant. Ford issued bulletins for vacuum leaks causing lean codes on these vans.
issues.next: Have the intake area smoke-tested and the cooling system pressure-tested. Fix it soon, because coolant mixing into the oil can damage the bearings.

issues.t: Cruise control switch can catch fire (recall)
issues.sym: A burning smell or smoke near the brake master cylinder, or cruise control or brake lights that stop working. A fire can start even when the van is parked.
issues.why: The speed control deactivation switch can leak brake fluid into its electrical side and overheat. Ford recalled millions of vehicles, including the Windstar, to add a fused wiring jumper.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 09V-399. If it was never done, have a Ford dealer do it and avoid parking the van in a garage until then.

issues.t: Shudder or slipping from torque converter
issues.sym: A shake or shudder at highway speed or when shifting into top gear, like driving over rumble strips. A check engine light may come on.
issues.why: The torque converter clutch inside the transmission wears and stops locking up smoothly. Ford issued bulletins for this shudder and for converter clutch codes on these vans.
issues.next: Have the codes read and the fluid checked. A fluid change sometimes helps a mild shudder, but a worn converter has to be replaced.

issues.t: Power sliding door stops working
issues.sym: The power sliding door won't open or close, stops partway, reverses, or doesn't latch fully.
issues.why: The power sliding door motor, cables, latch and track wear out, and dirty door contacts cause faults. Ford put out several bulletins on power sliding door problems.
issues.next: Clean and lube the door track and contacts first. If it still fails, have a shop check the motor, cable and latch before replacing parts.

issues.t: Interior lights flicker and battery drains
issues.sym: Dome lights flash or stay on, the door-ajar light stays lit, and the battery goes dead overnight. Power locks and windows may act up too.
issues.why: Dirty or damp sliding door contacts and door switches can tell the van a door is open, which keeps lights on and drains the battery. Ford issued bulletins for flickering dome lamps and battery drain on these vans.
issues.next: Clean the sliding door contacts and check every door switch. If the battery keeps dying, have a shop run a parasitic draw test.

issues.t: Check engine light from EGR pressure sensor
issues.sym: Check engine light with EGR codes such as P0401, sometimes with a slight hesitation. Otherwise the van may drive normally.
issues.why: The EGR pressure (DPFE) sensor and its hoses fail on these vans. Ford gave extra warranty coverage on this sensor for 2000-2003 models, which shows how common it was.
issues.next: Have the codes read. The sensor and its rubber hoses are a fairly cheap fix, and the van may not pass an emissions test until it is done.

issues.t: Rear A/C blows hot air
issues.sym: The rear air conditioning blows warm air out of the floor vents, or rear heat comes on when you select A/C.
issues.why: On many vans the rear climate control switch in the front console fails. Vacuum or blend door faults can cause the same complaint.
issues.next: Have the rear climate switch tested first, since it is the cheapest and most common fix.

issues.t: Fuel line connection can leak (recall)
issues.sym: A strong fuel smell or fuel dripping under the van.
issues.why: A fuel line connection can come apart and leak fuel, which could start a fire. Ford ran a safety campaign to fix it.
issues.next: If you smell fuel, don't drive it. Check your VIN for campaign 06E-056 with a Ford dealer.

issues.t: Second- and third-row seat latches may release (recall)
issues.sym: A rear bench seat that rattles, rocks or doesn't feel locked to the floor.
issues.why: The floor latches on the removable second- and third-row seats may not hold the seat in a crash. Ford recalled the vans to replace the latches.
issues.next: Make sure each rear seat clicks firmly into place, and check your VIN for recall 03V-459.

issues.t: Rear auxiliary blower motor can catch fire (recall)
issues.sym: A burning smell or smoke from the rear of the van when the rear A/C or heater fan is running.
issues.why: Wiring for the rear auxiliary A/C blower motor could overheat and start a fire. Ford recalled the vans to fix it.
issues.next: Turn off the rear fan if you smell burning, and check your VIN for recall 01V-262.

issues.t: Windshield wipers stop working (recall)
issues.sym: The front wipers stop, especially on the intermittent setting or when snow or ice keeps the blades from resting.
issues.why: The wiper switch could fail, leaving the driver without wipers. Ford recalled the vans to fix it.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 01V-261, and clear snow and ice off the blades before using the wipers.

issues.t: Rear wiring connector can short and melt (recall)
issues.sym: Tail lights, reverse sensors or trailer lights stop working, or a melted connector near the back of the van.
issues.why: A short in the rear wiring harness connector used for trailer towing could disable the rear lights and melt the connector. Ford recalled these vans.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 02V-072, especially if you tow.

issues.t: Adjustable pedals can catch on floor mat (recall)
issues.sym: The gas pedal sticks or doesn't come back up, with the pedals adjusted all the way and a floor mat in place.
issues.why: On vans with adjustable pedals, the accelerator could catch on the floor mat and hold the throttle open. Ford recalled the vans to fix it.
issues.next: Make sure the floor mat is secured and away from the pedals, and check your VIN for recall 01V-207.

issues.t: Van can roll away in Park (recall)
issues.sym: The van moves or rolls after being shifted into Park if the parking brake isn't set.
issues.why: The transmission park pawl might not engage, so the van acts as if it is in neutral. Ford recalled the vans to fix it.
issues.next: Always set the parking brake, and check your VIN for recall 96V-086.

issues.t: Hood panel can separate (recall)
issues.sym: A hood that flutters, rattles or seems loose at speed.
issues.why: The outer hood panel could come apart from the inner frame and fly up. Ford recalled the vans to fix it.
issues.next: Don't drive at highway speed with a loose hood. Check your VIN for recall 97V-180.

issues.t: Brake fluid leak and longer stops (recall)
issues.sym: The red brake warning light comes on, the pedal feels lower, or the van takes longer to stop.
issues.why: A brake fluid leak could reduce braking power. Ford recalled the vans to fix it.
issues.next: If the red brake light comes on, check the fluid and have the brakes inspected before driving. Check your VIN for recall 02V-101.

issues.t: Catalytic converter can ignite transmission fluid (recall)
issues.sym: Smoke or a burning smell from under the van, especially after a transmission fluid leak.
issues.why: The catalytic converter could get hot enough to ignite transmission fluid that dripped on it. Ford recalled these vans.
issues.next: Fix any transmission fluid leak right away and check your VIN for recall 97V-097.

issues.t: Loose front brake caliper bolts (recall)
issues.sym: A clunk, rattle or vibration from the front brakes.
issues.why: The front brake caliper anchor bolts could work loose. Ford ran a campaign to tighten or replace them; the noise was the warning sign.
issues.next: Have the brakes checked if you hear a clunk when stopping, and check your VIN for campaign 98I-003.

issues.t: Rear brakes drag in wet or icy weather
issues.sym: The van feels like the brakes are stuck on after sitting in rain or freezing weather, sometimes with a groan or a pop when it frees up.
issues.why: Moisture in the rear drum brakes can make the shoes stick to the drums. Ford issued bulletins on rear drum brake drag in wet or freezing conditions.
issues.next: Have the rear drums cleaned, adjusted and checked for leaking wheel cylinders. Replace shoes or hardware if they are worn.

issues.t: Power steering fluid leak at the rack
issues.sym: Power steering fluid drips near the front wheels, the fluid level keeps dropping, or the steering whines or feels heavy.
issues.why: The seals at the ends of the steering rack can leak. Ford issued a bulletin for this leak on these vans.
issues.next: Keep the fluid topped up and have the rack inspected. A leaking rack is usually replaced with a rebuilt unit.

issues.t: Heater core leak
issues.sym: A sweet coolant smell inside, a foggy windshield, wet carpet on the passenger side, or coolant that keeps going down.
issues.why: The heater core behind the dash can leak. Ford issued a bulletin for heater core leaks on these vans.
issues.next: Have the cooling system pressure-tested. Breathing coolant fumes isn't healthy, so don't put this off.
